_: Sources under .moon-data-cache/zoom/ for the photo maps of the moons that ship as procedural balls today, plus the sharper re-bases for the Galileans and Pluto. Same contract as gen-tiles.sources.json: the SHA-256 is what the shipped assets were cut from, and a re-downloaded product whose digest moved must not silently re-cut a map. Every product here is NASA or USGS and public domain; the citation field carries the credit line the product page asks for. Read `longitude` before writing any job: only Ganymede and Pluto are laid out the way an equirect texture is normally sampled (0E at the left edge, east increasing rightward) - eleven of the fifteen need a roll, a mirror, or both - and the reading comes from the product's own PDS3/ISIS3 label wherever one exists. The Astropedia catalog page is NOT reliable for it: its Dione and Tethys entries say Positive West where both labels say EAST. `wire` is the measured cost of one representative 4096x2048 candidate encoded both ways, so a rung can be priced before it is cut.
_gaps: What this file does NOT know, stated once so it is not rediscovered as a bug. (1) Mimas, Miranda and Ariel ship no label of any kind - Mimas' layout is measured off a gazetteer feature and holds, Miranda's and Ariel's are UNKNOWN and must be settled visually before either is baked. (2) Miranda and Ariel are 1440x720 and cover the southern hemisphere only; a 4K rung for either would be pure upsampling, so 2K is their honest ceiling and the rest is the procedural blend. (3) Titan is 4040 px because the only sharper USGS product is 1.5 GB and not global. (4) Ten of the fifteen are mono; keeping Io's and Ganymede's colour is free, everything else needs a colour pass keyed to a published true-colour reference if it is not to render grey.
_wire: Each `wire` block is one 4096x2048 candidate cut from the source with sharp 0.35.4 (fit: fill, kernel lanczos3, forced to 3-channel sRGB so both encoders see the same picture), then encoded as webp quality 85 effort 5 (the photo idiom in tools/encode-textures.mjs) and as UASTC KTX2 with the flags tools/gen-ktx2.mjs uses (-uastc -uastc_level 2 -uastc_rdo_l 1.0 -uastc_rdo_d 8192 -ktx2_zstandard_level 18 -mipmap -mip_filter box -y_flip). basisu from @gpu-tex-enc/basis, darwin-arm64. The candidates and containers are kept beside the sources in .moon-data-cache/zoom/wire/.

Uranus_Miranda_nasa3d.tif.product: NASA 3D Resources "Uranus - Miranda" image texture, 1440x720 TIFF (3 bands, greyscale content), Voyager 2 mosaic
Uranus_Miranda_nasa3d.tif.citation: USGS/Tammy Becker & JPL/Caltech - "From the USGS; a mosaic using Voyager imagery. From the JPL database of generated planetary maps." NASA imagery, public domain.

longitude.derivation: UNKNOWN - this texture ships no label and no metadata page beyond a credit line. Measured against the coronae, two layouts fit equally well: (a) east-positive with the left edge at 0E, which makes the banded feature at x/W 0.21 Arden Corona (29.1S, 73.7E) and the ringed oval at x/W 0.69 Elsinore (44.8S, 257.3E); (b) east-positive with the left edge at 180E, which swaps the two identifications. Telling Arden from Elsinore by eye is not reliable, so this stays UNKNOWN and must be settled in the alignment pass against a published feature.

Uranus_Miranda_nasa3d.tif.notes: PARTIAL COVERAGE, as expected: only the southern hemisphere is imaged and the unphotographed north is black no-data, with the data edge running between the equator and about 25S depending on longitude. Verona Rupes and the coronae are present. At 1440x720 this is the lowest-resolution source in the set - a 4K rung would be a pure 2.8x upsample, so a 2K map is the honest ceiling for this body and the rest has to come from the procedural blend.

Uranus_Ariel_nasa3d.tif.product: NASA 3D Resources "Uranus - Ariel" image texture, 1440x720 TIFF (3 bands, greyscale content), Voyager 2 mosaic
Uranus_Ariel_nasa3d.tif.citation: USGS/Tammy Becker & JPL/Caltech - "From the USGS; a mosaic using Voyager imagery. From the JPL database of generated planetary maps." NASA imagery, public domain.

longitude.derivation: UNKNOWN - no label, no metadata page beyond a credit line. Ariel's named chasmata cluster between 246E and 5E (Kachina 33.7S/246.0E, Kewpie, Brownie, Korrigan, Pixie), and the canyon network on this map runs from x/W 0.10 to 0.56. A plain 0-360E left-to-right reading puts that network at 37E-200E, where Ariel has no named chasmata, so that reading is probably wrong; a left-edge-180E reading (216E through 21E) fits the gazetteer. Not conclusive on one feature family, so it stays UNKNOWN and must be settled in the alignment pass.

Uranus_Ariel_nasa3d.tif.notes: PARTIAL COVERAGE, as expected: southern hemisphere only, unimaged north is black no-data. Chasma network and the bright cratered terrain are present. 1440x720, same ceiling as Miranda - a 2K map, not a 4K rung.
